notes: LT-03.2a finite rule-input => target/name/reason oracle plus target resolver oracles. Every expected value is literal data; no matcher is implemented. target_stem/suffix are recorded only to trace the DICT-05 concatenation invariant.

rule_scenarios.reason: archive.tar.gz has last suffix .gz; fixed stem Archive plus .gz gives Archive.gz.
.env has no extension; the whole-field mask .env matches and the fixed stem has no suffix.
README is a whole-field exact mask and has no extension; the result is the fixed stem alone.
name. has a trailing dot but no extension suffix; the fixed stem is used alone.
invoice.TXT matches *invoice* (priority 10) and Data/*.TXT (priority 100); the smaller priority wins and the .TXT suffix keeps its original case.
The * in Reports/*.pdf crosses the slash before Text; the file matches the relative path and lands directly under Reports.
data.bin matches no published Atlas rule; without a scenario the file goes to manual review and no target is planned.
Nova rule set sees only Nova targets; the North/Reports relative mask matches and the .txt suffix is preserved.
The *.xlsx basename rule matches the South/Data file and the fixed stem receives the .xlsx suffix.
The mask invoice matches the whole basename invoice; no extension is present so the fixed stem is used alone.
The mask invoice is applied to the whole field, so my-invoice.txt does not match; a substring needs * on both sides.
The BASENAME *orion* rule cannot see Orion_2031 in the directory chain, so it does not fall back; only the RELATIVE_PATH rule matches Main.pdf.
* matches zero characters, so AtlasReports matches Atlas*Reports.
* matches the -Orion- run, so Atlas-Orion-Reports also matches Atlas*Reports.

The mask is applied to the whole relative path including the basename. In Archive*Reports/* the first * crosses the separators up to the Reports directory and the trailing /* matches summary.pdf, so the cross-slash positive holds.
Archive*Reports requires the whole field to end with Reports; the field ends with summary.pdf, so the trailing-only mask does not match and the cross-slash wildcard must not be anchored at the end.
? matches exactly one character, so Report1.pdf matches Report?.pdf.
? requires exactly one character, so Report.pdf does not match Report?.pdf.
? requires exactly one character, so Report12.pdf does not match Report?.pdf.
Both mask and match value slashes are normalized to \ for the matcher, so the backslash mask matches the canonical slash path.
Matching is case-insensitive, so CAFÉ.PDF matches the composed café.pdf; the .pdf suffix keeps its original lower-case form.
casefold does not apply NFC/NFKC, so the decomposed e + combining acute accent is not the composed é and does not match CAFÉ.PDF.
Both rules match priority-file.pdf; priority 1 is applied before priority 1000, so the larger numeric priority does not win.
Equal minimal priority with the same final target is not a conflict; attribution is stable by dictionary_id then rule_id, so dictionary-atlas-general wins.
Two matched rules share the minimal priority but plan different final targets (Reports vs Invoices), which is a conflict; no rule is selected and the row goes to manual review.
Only the last suffix .pdf is taken from report.v2.pdf; the fixed stem keeps its own dot, giving Final.Report.pdf.

target_scenarios.reason: The displayed synthetic path is a configured existing Atlas target and resolves to its logical root and relative directory.
A second configured Atlas directory resolves without creating anything.
The Nova company resolves only its own configured directory.
The path is under the allowed root but no configured directory exists; the resolver must not create it.
A DEMO path with a prefix other than the allowed DEMO:/SandboxRoot is outside the permitted root.
An empty path segment is not a valid RelativeDirectory; the request is rejected as a validation error.
Only the synthetic DEMO:/SandboxRoot scheme is accepted; a physical computer path is not an allowed target.
The Atlas target is not configured for Nova; the server checks the company scope before accepting the target.

invalid_rule_cases.reason: The Rule.mask schema pattern rejects **; it is not a second spelling of *.
mask has minLength 1, so an empty mask is rejected.
mask has maxLength 512, so a 513 character mask is rejected.
target_stem has minLength 1, so an empty fixed stem is rejected.
target_stem has maxLength 200; the server does not truncate it automatically.
target_stem must not contain a path separator.
target_stem must not contain a backslash separator.
target_stem must not contain control characters.
match_field must be BASENAME or RELATIVE_PATH; switching to another field is not supported.
target is required; a rule without a canonical target reference is rejected.
The mask language is not a regex; a regex expression is not a supported mask and is rejected at the domain level (the JSON Schema cannot express this).
There is no OR operator; a mask containing a hidden OR is not supported and is rejected at the domain level.
Wildcard escaping is not supported; the backslash-star escape is rejected at the domain level.
The rule is schema-valid but the target directory is not configured for the company; the server rejects it and does not create the directory.
A Nova rule may only reference Nova targets; the server checks the company scope before accepting the target.
